quotes: If the page is blocked by a robots.txt file or the crawler can't access the page, the crawler will never see the `noindex` rule, and the page can still appear in search results, for example if other pages link to it.
For the `noindex` rule to be effective, the page or resource must not be blocked by a robots.txt file, and it has to be otherwise accessible to the crawler.
value.theFactThatGovernsAnyFix: robots.txt Disallow DOES NOT REMOVE A PAGE FROM THE INDEX — it stops crawling. A disallowed URL can still be indexed from links and shown without a snippet, which is exactly why the 106 blocked pages carry 216 impressions. Removing a page from search needs noindex, and NOINDEX REQUIRES THE PAGE TO BE CRAWLABLE. Disallow and noindex are therefore mutually exclusive on the same URL.

title: Decide whether Googlebot should be blocked from the /from/ corridor leaves
finding: 106 URLs with 216 impressions in 28 days are Disallowed for Googlebot on four hosts
origin: The corridor Disallow arrived on 2026-07-20 as a template across three forks (867790a, 7fd0569, 6054ed4) and by hand in almi-portuguese on 2026-07-28 (489ca26). Extending it to Googlebot/Bingbot was a SEPARATE, LATER change: 5e3e211 and e462310 (2026-07-28), 0397abd (2026-08-09), and 489ca26 for portuguese.

optionA.action: Remove the DEEP_LEAVES entries from the Googlebot/Bingbot group only, leaving the `*` group as is.
optionA.expected: Googlebot may crawl the corridor leaves again. The ISR cost the original commit was reducing returns for those crawls.
optionA.rollback: Re-add the two DEEP_LEAVES strings to the Googlebot group. One-line revert per repo.

optionB.action: Keep the Disallow and ALSO remove those leaves from sitemap.ts.
optionB.expected: The sitemap stops advertising URLs robots.txt forbids. The 216 impressions decay as the index ages out.
optionB.note: almi-portuguese's own commit 489ca26 already records this as a KNOWN INCONSISTENCY: 'src/app/sitemap.ts still emits those leaves, so the sitemap now advertises URLs robots.txt forbids Google to fetch. Shrinking it to match is Nasir's call, not a side effect of a cost fix.'

the_trap: 🔴 Do NOT reach for noindex while the Disallow stands. Googlebot cannot see a noindex on a page it may not fetch.

title: Decide whether the 16-agent AI/SEO crawler block is still wanted
finding: 13 repos block the same 16 user-agents with Disallow: /

origin: Applied as a template on 2026-07-20 across 11 forks with a byte-identical commit message, plus almi-goethe (37ecdf1, same day) and almi-portuguese (489ca26, 8 days later) with bespoke messages.

optionA.expected: No AI-search citations from ChatGPT/Perplexity; no crawl cost from those agents.

optionB.action: Trim the AI-SEARCH agents (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot) from the list, keeping the TRAINING and SEO-backlink agents blocked.

open_question: 🔴 No commit explains why THESE 16, nor why AI-training crawlers are grouped with SEO backlink crawlers. That grouping decision is unexplained in the history.
